audit.whatIsWrong: Three rows contradicted the already-audited mirror. Ours read Swain / Swain / Swain / Swain / Skill / Skill / Skill; the mirror set L1-L3 Swain, L4-5 Dr. Mundo, L6 Swain, first item Dr. Mundo, 2+ items Skill.
audit.why: Mirrors must agree, and the mirror's version is also the one consistent with his kit: a 4s percent-health Bonesaw and passive regen own the 4-5 window, while Demonic Ascension's indefinite uptime is what takes level 6 back.
audit.corrected: Row 3 to Dr. Mundo, row 4 to Swain, row 5 to Dr. Mundo, as matched pairs, with ratings adjusted and whys[3], whys[4], whys[5] and mid rewritten so the prose no longer contradicts the chart.

audit.whatIsWrong: Heart Zapper is the tracked ability on every line and its cooldown never appears (17/16.5/16/15.5/15s), nor does Infected Bonesaw's 4s / 975 range. Demonic Ascension's uptime condition — it holds only while you are draining a champion inside 650 range — was also absent, and it is the reason level 6 is yours.
audit.why: 'Race his heal' is unusable; 'hold the drain on a champion inside 650' is a thing you can do.
audit.corrected: 17s, 4s / 975 range and the 650-range drain condition written into whys[4], mid, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and dontsFull[1].d.
sources: ownerKit Swain R text and 650 range

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most important interaction in this matchup is absent from all 40+ fields: Goes Where He Pleases resists the FIRST immobilizing effect that hits him. Swain's entire pattern is one root — so his passive eats your opening Nevermove outright and drops a cannister he can walk over to heal and refresh it. The page instead tells you 'Mundo has no dash to escape the hand', which reads as though the root is free.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Dr. Mundo resists the first Immobilizing effect that hits him, instead losing Health and dropping a chemical cannister nearby. Dr. Mundo can pick it up ... restoring Health and reducing this Ability's Cooldown.'
audit.corrected: spikes[0].text, report[5].t and breakdown.cooldowns now state that your first root is spent breaking the passive and that denying the cannister pickup matters. Blunt Force Trauma's auto reset added to dontsFull[0].d.
sources: enemyKit Dr. Mundo P text and hardCC flag

edits.before: Each successful E-root-pull chain collects Soul Fragments that permanently stack your max HP, compounding an advantage his Q ranks and passive regen cannot fully erase at this stage.
edits.after: Infected Bonesaw ranks up on a 4s cooldown and his passive regen refunds your chip faster than fragments stack, so 4-5 slips to him unless Grievous Wounds is already online.

edits.before: Maximum Dosage is live and directly races your Demonic Ascension drain — whichever R goes up second gets raced by the first, making this stage a genuine coin-flip depending on R timing.
edits.after: Both ultimates are live, but Demonic Ascension holds indefinitely as long as you keep draining a champion inside 650 range — bait Maximum Dosage out first and level 6 is yours.

edits.before: Luden's sharpens your W poke into burst that stacks on Mundo's own Q percent-HP drain, but he is building Warmog's now and the window to convert this into a kill is closing fast.
edits.after: Your first item sharpens W poke, but his goes into raw health and his own regen — the first-item stage belongs to him, and the window to convert your lane lead is closing fast.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are your clearest ownership window: each E-root-pull-Q repetition adds Soul Fragments and permanently widens your HP pool while his Q ranks increase his cleaver poke but cannot out-trade your fragment stacking. Force short fights where your burst lands before his passive regen kicks in, then back off before he can sustain through the damage. At Level 6 the lane flattens out hard — Maximum Dosage is a combat R that heals him for a massive percentage of his health mid-fight, which directly races your Demonic Ascension drain; never pop your R while his is available, because the two healing windows cancel and he wins the extended fight on base stats.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 slip away from you: Infected Bonesaw is a 4-second percent-health throw at 975 range and his passive regen refunds chip faster than your fragments stack, so take short fights only once Heart Zapper (17s at rank 1) has already burst, never while it is storing your damage. Force the exchange where your burst lands, then back off before the regen catches up. At Level 6 the lane swings back to you — Demonic Ascension holds indefinitely as long as you keep draining a champion inside 650 range — but Maximum Dosage instantly heals a percentage of his missing health, so bait it out first and commit with Grievous Wounds already online.

edits.before: Your E-root into W-slow into Q-burst combo comes fully online and Mundo has no dash to escape the hand — fish the root to chunk him and collect Soul Fragments before his passive regen catches up.
edits.after: Your W-slow into E-root into Q-burst comes online and Mundo has no dash — but his passive resists the first immobilise and drops a cannister, so the opening root is spent breaking that, not landing it.

edits.before: Track Dr. Mundo's Heart Zapper: His sustain + reset. Anti-heal it. When it is down — E-root + R him.
edits.after: His passive resists the first immobilise — your first E is spent breaking it. Deny the cannister pickup.

edits.before: - Dr. Mundo Heart Zapper: matchup-defining — His sustain + reset. Anti-heal it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Dr. Mundo Heart Zapper: matchup-defining — 17s at rank 1; it stores your damage and heals it back, so anti-heal it. His passive eats your first root. - Your E: 12s, never on chip. - Your ultimate: kill windows only.

edits.before: His sustain + reset. Anti-heal it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Heart Zapper stores your damage for 17s and heals it back. Anti-heal it.

edits.before: That is Dr. Mundo's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Blunt Force Trauma resets his auto — the wind-up is the tell, not the cast.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Infected Bonesaw is a 4s, 975-range percent-health throw. Sidestep it.

notes: The passive immobilise-resist is the headline find here and it was missing from every field on the page. Note also that 'Q cleavers' (dontsFull[1].t) is a Darius/Garen-flavoured phrase for a single-target Bonesaw throw, and the Level 1 rating of 8/10 sits oddly beside whys[0] calling the stage 'a wash' — both are under or near the applier's 25-character skip threshold, so neither is worth an edit; flagging instead. Warmog's / Luden's / Shadowflame / Liandry's references are unverified 26.15 itemisation. packet.suspectNames flagged 'Bait Maximum Dosage' — false positive, that is his real R.
